text:
leo: quick question — onboarding Lynx-3B (community release) for evals. license page says: https://example.com/lynx3b-license — seems to require attribution and disallows resale. can we publish quantized weights for Dedicated/private deployments?
amanda: can you paste the specific clause?
jordan: short answers usually: hosting via our API is fine, redistribution (downloading binaries) gets tricky. but depends on license language re: derivative works and redistribution.
sarah-legal: I skimmed the license. key bits: Section 2.c requires attribution in product docs; Section 4.a prohibits redistribution of the model weights in unmodified form to third parties for commercial use; Section 4.b is ambiguous on transformed/quantized artifacts.
sarah-legal: critical distinction: if a quantized file is a derivative work under their license, then distributing it (e.g., giving customer a tar with q8 weights) likely triggers redistribution restrictions.
leo: so is it safe to include quantized weights in a Dedicated running in a customer's VPC? that's not "redistribution" in the public sense — we're just deploying to their infra.
sarah-legal: deploying into a customer's VPC counts as providing the model to the customer but not public redistribution. Clause 4.a seems tailored to preventing third-party resale; so Dedicated in-customer is usually ok if customer is the licensee and we have a compatible contract. for Hosted API we also shouldn't publish downloadable artifacts.
nora: what about delivering a docker image with the quantized weights to an enterprise customer as part of a Private on-prem package? that would be shipping the binary.
sarah-legal: shipping a container that contains the quantized weights is distribution. need explicit permission or an enterprise addendum. two options: 1) get a redistribution grant from the model owners, or 2) obfuscate the weights and provide a closed-host runtime where weights never leave our control (i.e., we run it for them).
jordan: practically, option 2 is sometimes infeasible for air-gapped on-prem customers who require self-hosted binaries. for those we should escalate to legal for a carve-out.
amanda: also: attribution requirement — they want a visible credit line in product docs and UI. is that mandatory for private deployments too?
sarah-legal: yes, attribution applies across uses unless license says otherwise. we should add a checklist entry: add a docs banner and include attribution in the EULA/credits for customer deliveries.
leo: on the technical side: we tried 8-bit quant and produced q8 weights. engineers want to publish quantized model optimizations and FLOPS/latency benchmarks internally and to customers. is publishing benchmarks OK or does that leak model IP?
jordan: benchmarks (latency, perplexity on standard sets) are fine. do not publish extracted tokenizer vocab files or raw weight diffs that would reconstruct the model.
sarah-legal: confirm: benchmarks are allowed but include attribution; ensure any shared artifacts don't include weight binaries.
leo: sample packaging command we'd use to make a downloadable bundle: ```tar czf lynx3b-q8-20240301.tar.gz model/quantized/lynx3b_q8.bin LICENSE.txt``` — so we shouldn't hand that to customers unless we have redistribution rights, correct?
sarah-legal: correct. do not distribute that tar to customers without express redistribution rights.
nora: timeline: we have one pilot enterprise that wants the on-prem container next quarter. I'll flag this as a blocker for the onboarding runbook.
amanda: action items?
sarah-legal: (1) I'll draft an internal license summary and call out whether quantized artifacts are derivatives under their license and what approvals we need. target EOD +2 days. (2) For the pilot, we should request a redistribution addendum from the model owner — I'll prepare a templated request.
jordan: engineering: add gating to the onboarding flow: checkbox "redistribution rights obtained" before allowing packaging artifacts. I'll open a PR on the runbook.
leo: I'll hold off publishing q8 weights to the private repo. can we host the model as a service instead and share only API endpoints for the pilot?
sarah-legal: yes, recommend hosting in our Dedicated/private offering and include attribution. for the on-prem case, escalate.
deploy-bot: new ticket created: ENGML-4823 "Lynx-3B redistribution review + runbook gate" assigned to jordan, nora, sarah-legal
leo: thanks all. tagging @sarah-legal again — please ping when the summary is up. :pray:
